requirements.title: Real-Time Item Delivery Under 1 Second via WebSocket
requirements.description: When an item is pushed to the server, a delivery notification and item metadata (including download URL for files or full content for text snippets) are pushed to all relevant connected trusted devices over a persistent WebSocket connection within 1 second for payloads under 10 MB. The WebSocket connection is authenticated using the same scenario-authenticator token validation. The server maintains a per-connection authenticated session and will not deliver items to unauthenticated or untrusted connections.

validation.notes: Unit test: presence hub fan-out correctly identifies all connected, trusted WebSocket sessions for a given owner and excludes the sender
Unit test: WebSocket upgrade handler validates bearer token with scenario-authenticator before accepting the connection
Unit test: delivery message schema includes item_id, type, retention_policy, download_url or content, and timestamp
Unit test: fan-out is skipped for sessions whose device_id is not in the current trust group (handles concurrent revocation)
Integration test: Device A uploads a 1 MB file; measure time from upload completion to Device B receiving the WebSocket delivery event; assert < 1 second
Integration test: Device A sends a text snippet; Device B receives WebSocket push with full snippet content < 1 second
Integration test: unauthenticated WebSocket upgrade attempt is rejected with HTTP 401
Integration test: revoked device's WebSocket connection does not receive delivery events after revocation
p99 delivery latency < 1 second for items ≤ 10 MB under simulated 10-device concurrent send load
WebSocket connection establishment completes within 500 ms including auth validation
Smoke test: send an item from Device A; observe it appears in Device B's Receive pane without manual refresh

requirements.title: Device Online/Offline Presence Visibility
requirements.description: Each trusted device's online or offline presence is tracked server-side based on active WebSocket connections and surfaced in the UI. The Receive pane and Device Management views display a presence indicator for each device. Presence state transitions (connect/disconnect) are broadcast to all other trusted devices in the same trust group over the existing WebSocket channel within 1 second. Presence state is not persisted across server restarts and is always derived from live connection state.

validation.notes: Unit test: presence hub correctly marks a device as online on WebSocket connect and offline on disconnect or connection drop
Unit test: presence change event is enqueued for broadcast to all other trusted devices in the same trust group
Unit test: presence state is not read from a persistent store; it is always computed from the live connection registry
Integration test: Device B connects; Device A's UI receives a presence-online event for Device B within 1 second
Integration test: Device B disconnects; Device A's UI receives a presence-offline event for Device B within 1 second
Integration test: revoked device's presence is marked offline and removed from all peers' presence views
Presence state change propagation to all peers completes within 1 second
Playbook: open two browser tabs as two devices; toggle one offline; confirm presence indicator updates in the other tab
Accessibility: presence indicators expose aria-label='Device [name] online' or 'offline'
